title: Give thanks (1 Chronicles 16:8)
hookLine: "O give thanks unto the LORD, call upon His name", David's song for the ark
carry: make known his doings among the peoples

cards: The ark of the covenant, the gold-covered chest that held the tablets, has been away for years: captured in battle, sent back, kept for months in one family's house. Now King David brings it up to Jerusalem.
Music, shouting, the sound of horns. David himself dances. When the ark is set down in the tent he's pitched for it, there are offerings, and bread and cakes for everyone in the crowd.
Then David does something meant to outlast the day. He puts singers in place, and hands them a song that begins with two Hebrew words: hodu ladonai.

teach.b: The Book of Chronicles gives the song in full. In the old Jewish translation it opens: "O give thanks unto the LORD, call upon His name; make known His doings among the peoples."
Near its end comes a line that runs all through Jewish prayer: "O give thanks unto the LORD; for He is good; for His mercy endureth for ever." The song is a weave.
Its opening lines also appear in Psalm one hundred five, its middle in Psalm ninety-six, its close in Psalm one hundred six. Chronicles stitches them together for one great day.
In the Ashkenazi prayer book, the passage comes right after Baruch She'amar; in many Sephardi prayer books, just before it. Either way, a morning of song begins where David began: with thanks.
Notice the second half of that first verse: make known his doings among the peoples. Thanks here isn't only a private feeling. It's said out loud, so others hear the story.
And hodu, give thanks, carries an echo.
In Genesis, when Leah names her fourth son, she says: this time I will praise the LORD.

teach.h: JUDAH: THIS TIME I WILL PRAISE.
teach.b: His name is Judah, Yehudah, built from that same root. The tribe of Judah carries that name, and the word Jew comes from it too, through Yehudi.
So a word for giving thanks sits close to the name the people carry.

how: Hodu, from 1 Chronicles 16, is said each morning in the verses of song: after Baruch She'amar in the Ashkenazi rite, and before it in many Sephardi rites.

o: feel grateful quietly, keeping it to yourself
pay back a favor so no debt is left
thank God out loud, so others hear the story

p: brought home to Jerusalem by David

s: the song in Chronicles appears nowhere else in the Bible
it weaves together parts of Psalms 105, 96 and 106.
Ashkenazi and Sephardi prayer books place hodu in the same spot
after Baruch She'amar in the Ashkenazi rite; before it in many Sephardi rites.

games.q: you're King David. the ark is set down in Jerusalem, the offerings are made and the bread handed out. what do you do next?
o: start building a palace for yourself.
send the army out to celebrate.
games.why: he puts Asaph and the Levites in place to give thanks, and hands them a song: O give thanks unto the LORD, call upon His name.

practice: Think of one person who did something good for you lately and didn't get much credit, a coworker who covered for you, a neighbor, a sibling, and shape one specific sentence of thanks you could say in front of others: not thanks for everything, but thanks for this.
If you pray, you can say hodu ladonai, give thanks to the LORD.

wordCard.voice: Give thanks. Hodu: David's song for the ark, sung each morning near the start of the verses of song.

orig.note: Hebrew: give thanks, the root shared with Yehudah, Judah.

carryVoice: Your line: make known his doings among the peoples. In this song, thanks is meant to be heard. Until tomorrow.
